# 1 Clement Chapter 37 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 37 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_037_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 37

**37:1** Let us therefore serve as soldiers, brothers, with all earnestness, under his faultless commands.

**37:2** Let us consider those who serve under our military commanders: how orderly, how ready, how readily they carry out orders.

**37:3** Not all are generals, nor tribunes, nor centurions, nor commanders of fifty, and so on; but each in his own rank carries out the commands of the emperor and of the commanders.

**37:4** The great cannot exist without the small, nor the small without the great; there is a certain blending in all things, and in this lies the advantage.

**37:5** Let us take our body as an example. The head is nothing without the feet, and the feet are nothing without the head. The smallest members of the body are necessary and useful to the whole body; and all the members together breathe with one accord and are united in a single submission, for the preservation of the whole body.

---

*LOGOS preserves the precise Roman military rank terminology (general, tribune, centurion, commander of fifty) which grounds the analogy in contemporary Roman imperial reality.*
